title: Effectiveness of an fpqc descent datum is local on the total space
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a descent datum relative to a surjective quasi-compact flat morphism X to S is effective as soon as it is locally effective on the total space, that is, as soon as every point of V lies in an open W which the datum carries into X times W and over which the restricted datum is effective (statement lines 9144-9152). The proof glues the local realisations. It covers V by such opens, chooses for each a scheme U_i over S with an isomorphism of descent data from the canonical datum of X times U_i to the restricted datum on W_i, and then, for each pair of indices, applies descent along the fpqc covering X to S to the open subscheme of X times U_i obtained as the preimage under that isomorphism of the overlap of W_i and W_j, producing opens U_ij of U_i with the expected description (proof lines 9155-9167). Since the identity of the overlap is compatible with descent data it descends to a unique morphism between these opens, and the resulting data are glueing data for schemes, so the U_i glue to a single scheme U over S (proof lines 9168-9177); pulling back along X and using the chosen isomorphisms produces the required isomorphism from X times U to V (proof lines 9178-9179). The claim is H2: two descent steps are used in earnest, one to recognise the overlaps as pullbacks of opens downstairs and one to descend the gluing morphisms, and the argument is displayed in full.
